sources.title: Robert M. Gray, Source Coding Theory, first edition

contents.name: §5.1 finite codebook, nearest-neighbor cells and Voronoi regions
contents.detail: The source supplies the nearest-neighbor quantizer convention; the local definition adds the explicit least-index tie cells and measurable finite-valued map.

contents.name: §5.2 centroid reproduction and fixed-cell squared-error cost
contents.detail: The centroid condition is stated in the source; the local identity proves the exact weighted finite-data excess term.

contents.name: §5.2–§5.3 high-rate approximations and overload-region qualification
contents.detail: The source's approximation motivates the topic but does not prove this compact exact limit; the local uniform Taylor and Riemann-sum proof supplies the stronger restricted claim.

contents.name: §5.6 Holder optimization of the fixed-rate high-rate point density
contents.detail: The source gives the point-density optimization principle; the local proof verifies the exact positive C1 compact class and its unique equality case.

contents.name: General vector and overload-region high-rate formulas
contents.reason: The assigned theorem is only the exact positive C1 one-dimensional compact compander limit; no vector formula, unbounded support, negligible-overload approximation, or unrestricted optimal quantizer claim is included.

sources.read_locator: Complete 197-page author-hosted book PDF inspected at Chapter 5 §§5.1–5.3 and §5.6; the finite nearest-cell setup, high-rate/overload qualifications, and Holder point-density optimization were read in full. The book explicitly calls its high-rate development less rigorous; the local compact theorem is proved independently.
sources.extent: Full author-hosted textbook PDF and extracted text, 197 PDF pages / 188 printed pages. Relevant sections were inspected in the complete text; no claim is made that unrelated chapters were reread during this batch.
sources.support: Textbook treatment of finite quantizer cells, squared-error distortion, high-rate approximations, overload caveats, and point-density optimization. It does not discharge the local finite Lloyd, global exhaustive, or exact compact Taylor proofs.

sources.title: Robert Gallager, 6.450 Principles of Digital Communications I, Chapter 3: Quantization
sources.locator: §§3.2.1–3.2.3, printed pp. 65–68; §3.7 and Appendix 3A, printed pp. 73–81.

contents.name: §3.2.1 nearest representation point minimizes fixed-codebook squared error
contents.detail: The nearest-center convention is retained with a deterministic least-index tie rule.

contents.name: §3.2.2 conditional means minimize fixed-cell squared error
contents.detail: The conditional-mean principle motivates the result; the local proof supplies the weighted finite-sample identity and uniqueness.

contents.name: §3.2.3 Lloyd-Max alternating update procedure
contents.detail: The source gives the alternating nearest-region/conditional-mean route; the local algorithm fixes finite weights, exact tie handling, unchanged empty centers and exact stopping.

contents.name: §3.2.3 Lloyd-Max distortion descent and termination discussion
contents.detail: The source's continuous-source epsilon-stopping discussion is not used as a finite-termination proof; the local theorem proves strict descent and termination from a finite center-state set.

contents.name: §3.2.3 Example 3.2.1: a continuous-source local Lloyd-Max minimum
contents.detail: The source motivates the local-versus-global warning; the B-page counterexample supplies a separate exact five-point empirical witness.

contents.name: Appendix 3A high-rate nonuniform scalar approximation
contents.detail: The appendix gives an approximate high-rate model; the local proof replaces that approximation with the exact stated compact C1 limit.

sources.read_locator: Complete 24-page Chapter 3 PDF retrieved and text-extracted. §§3.2.1–3.2.3, printed pp. 65–68, and §3.7/Appendix 3A, printed pp. 72–81, were inspected in full, including the fixed-codebook nearest-center argument, conditional-mean minimization, Lloyd steps, continuous-source local-minimum example, and high-rate approximation discussion.
sources.extent: Full 24-page course chapter PDF, extracted with MuPDF text rendering; displayed equations and the exact finite-data refinements were checked against the source text and local derivations.
sources.support: Independent lecture-note treatment of scalar nearest-center cells, centroid updates, Lloyd-Max iteration, local optima, and high-rate quantization. Its continuous-density convergence discussion does not prove finite-state exact termination for the empirical algorithm here.

sources.title: Robert M. Gray and David L. Neuhoff, Quantization, IEEE Transactions on Information Theory 44(6) (1998)
sources.locator: §II, printed pp. 2328–2330; §III, printed pp. 2340–2343; §IV-A, printed pp. 2344–2346.

contents.name: §III finite quantizer encoders, partitions, codebooks and squared-error distortion
contents.detail: The finite encoder/partition setup and squared-error convention are adopted, with a local Borel and finite-second-moment contract.

contents.name: §III nearest-neighbor and centroid optimality conditions
contents.detail: The source states both conditions; the local finite weighted identity proves the centroid excess exactly.

contents.name: §II Lloyd Method I and possible local optima
contents.detail: The alternating design route is retained; the local proof gives the finite exact procedure and its own finite-state termination argument.

contents.name: §IV-A Bennett integral, compander point density and small-cell assumptions
contents.detail: The source explicitly presents Bennett's formula as an approximation requiring small, slowly varying cells; the local compact C1 Taylor proof establishes the exact restricted limit without importing vector or overload claims.

contents.name: §IV-A Panter–Dite optimal scalar point density
contents.detail: The source supports the f^(1/3) point-density formula; the local proof proves its unique minimum within the stated compact C1 class.

sources.read_locator: Complete 59-page survey PDF retrieved and text-extracted. §II, printed pp. 2328–2330, §III, printed pp. 2340–2343, and §IV-A, printed pp. 2344–2346, were inspected in full for Lloyd history/optimality, finite quantizer structure, Bennett integral, point density, and explicit approximation assumptions.
sources.extent: Full 59-page IEEE survey PDF and extracted text; the cited sections and their full surrounding reasoning were inspected.
sources.support: Independent survey treatment of quantizer definitions, Lloyd local/global distinctions, compander point density and high-resolution formulas. The authors state the Bennett formula is approximate and list small-cell and other assumptions; the exact compact result is proved locally.

pages.source_context: The companion examples use the three independently read full-text treatments recorded on the A page; their exact finite calculations are proved locally.

supported_examples.detail: Every distance comparison, centroid, distortion and strict inequality is computed exactly in the counterexample proof.
The midpoint-cell integral is evaluated exactly for every N and compared to the compact theorem coefficient.
